name: Sandbox: isolation boundary around running code
panels: Some untrusted code (a file) is about to run on the computer, next to the user's private files.
A dashed boundary (a zone) is drawn around the code. The code runs inside it.
The code tries to reach the user's private files outside the boundary; a gate at the edge blocks it.
The code can only use one allowed thing inside the boundary; the user's files stay safe.

name: Config loader with schema validation
panels: A config file is read from disk by the loader.
The loader checks the config against a schema.
Bad config: a wrong field is rejected with an error and the app does not start.
Good config: the checked settings are handed to the app and it starts.

name: Rate limiting
panels: Several clients send requests to an API.
A rate limiter sits in front of the API and counts requests per client.
One client goes over its limit: its extra requests are rejected with 429.
The next time window starts: the counter resets and requests pass again.

name: Retries with backoff
panels: A client calls a server and the call fails.
The client waits 1 second, retries and fails again.
It waits longer each time (2 s, then 4 s) before the next try.
A later retry succeeds and the client carries on.

name: Queue with workers
panels: A producer adds jobs to a queue.
Jobs line up in the queue while the workers are idle.
Each worker takes one job from the queue.
Workers finish and send results to storage; the queue gets shorter.

name: Database migration
panels: The app uses a database with the old schema (v1).
A migration script (v1 to v2) is written and a backup of the database is taken.
The script runs and changes the database tables to v2.
The new app version runs against the database on schema v2.
